_comment: Tunables for case_timeline.py --tempo (operator_tempo.py): the hour-of-day x weekday read of WHEN an operator acts. Adapted from the 'two distinct activity rhythms' timing read in the Packt ACTIH companion repo (MIT, (c) 2026 Packt) [PK Packt ACTIH companion repo, 2026, chapter-03 threat-profile deliverable]; the event filter, the offset scan, the abstention floor and the two-rhythm residue test are our adaptation. Output is LEAD-ONLY: it never feeds attribution, clustering or KB edges. Keep the after-hours window aligned with analysis/signature-catalog.md T-02.

settings._comment: min_events/min_distinct_days = the abstention floor (below it the read is 'insufficient'); top_n = offsets reported; consistent_margin = offsets within this share of the best form the reported range; min_working_share = below it no offset concentrates activity ('no_clear_window'); burst_collapse_minutes = same kind+host events closer than this are ONE decision; drop_midnight_exact = a 00:00:00 stamp is date-only precision, not an action at midnight; two_rhythm_* = the second-band test, built on HOURS ONLY (weekday/weekend is reported per band as an attribute, never as a band): residue = events outside the primary working hours on any day; it must hold max(min_events, min_share x n) events, and min_working_share of it must sit in one working-window-wide band whose start is at least the window width (circular hours) from the primary band's start, so the two bands never overlap; min_coverage_gain = primary band + second band must beat the best single window-wide band of hours by at least max(min_events, this share x n) events, otherwise the read is one rhythm.

working_window._comment: Local business window scored per candidate offset. Hours are [start, end) local; days are Python weekday numbers (0 = Monday). A Sun-Thu work week is [6, 0, 1, 2, 3].

after_hours_window._comment: Second window, any weekday. 23:00-06:00 local matches signature-catalog T-02 (Off-Timezone Clustering) so a posting-time read and an operator-tempo read use the same definition of 'off hours'.

offsets._comment: Candidate UTC offsets in hours, -12 to +14 including the half/quarter-hour zones in common use.

operator_kinds._comment: Event kinds whose timestamp an operator plausibly chose or acted at. Used for `operator_events` rows ({when, kind, source, host?, url?}) in any input JSON and for commits read from github_harvest output (kind commit_author). A row whose kind is not listed is excluded with a reason.

entries.commit_author: git author time of a non-bot commit — the moment the author's client recorded the change
entries.post: a channel/forum/social post time taken from the platform record
entries.message: a direct or group message time
entries.panel_action: a manual action in an operator panel (ticket reply, deposit approval, config change) observed during an authorised engagement
entries.login_event: an interactive login seen in a log the analyst lawfully holds
entries.manual_registration: a registration the analyst has reason to believe was hand-placed (not drop-catch / bulk API)

timeline_kinds._comment: Disposition of each case_timeline event kind. include=true keeps it, false drops it with `reason`, 'issuer_check' keeps a certificate only if its issuer is not in automated_cert_issuers. An unlisted kind is dropped.

registration.reason: registrar-stamped purchase moment; drop-catch and bulk-API registrations are automated (confounder)

cert.reason: issuance time is operator-chosen only for a manually ordered certificate

whois_updated.reason: registrar/registry-side update (renewal, EPP status, transfer) — system-stamped

expired.reason: term end computed from the creation date, not an action

registrant_era.reason: WHOIS-history observation window — first/last seen, not acted

hosting.reason: passive-DNS observation window — sensor first/last seen, not acted

ns_era.reason: scanner observation window — first/last seen, not acted

archive_span.reason: Wayback crawl schedule, not operator activity

artifact_window.reason: Wayback crawl schedule, not operator activity

wayback_capture.reason: Wayback crawl or on-demand capture time

content_updated.reason: page self-declared date — CMS/server-generated and forgeable

automated_cert_issuers._comment: Case-insensitive substrings of a certificate issuer that mark automated (ACME / managed / AutoSSL) issuance — the timestamp is a renewal job's, not the operator's.

bot_identity_patterns._comment: Case-insensitive substrings of a commit author name/e-mail that mark an automated committer.

confounders._comment: Printed with EVERY tempo read, whatever the verdict.
values: automation or schedulers: cron jobs, CI pipelines, scheduled posts and certificate renewals fire at machine-chosen times (signature-catalog T-01 precision intervals are the tell)
shift work and outsourcing: a contracted or shift-based team keeps its client's hours, not its own
deliberate offsets or VPN: an operator aware of tempo analysis can delay or schedule actions; a VPN moves the apparent location, not the clock
DST: a fixed UTC offset cannot follow a daylight-saving change, so a set spanning one splits across adjacent offsets
mixed team: people in several zones produce a blended or bimodal histogram
platform server time: some platforms stamp events with server, queue or rounded time rather than the moment the operator acted
regional work week: the default window assumes Mon-Fri; a Sun-Thu or six-day week shifts the weekday share
collection sampling: collectors keep first/last commits or recent posts, so one period can dominate the set
